author: C

components.title: Allocate sold units to lots using FIFO
components.what: Sequentially allocate the six sales (78, 67, 103, 115, 113, 32 = 508 total units) against lots 1-8 in order, tracking units taken from each lot until all 508 units are consumed.

components.title: Calculate cost per lot consumed
components.what: Multiply units taken from each lot by that lot's unit cost.

components.title: Sum total COGS
components.what: Add all lot cost contributions to get total cost of goods sold to the nearest cent.

challenges.problem: If individual sales orders require per-sale COGS recording and rounding to the nearest cent, batching sales could theoretically hide per-transaction rounding differences or order-fulfillment boundary allocations
Some accounting contexts define Cost of Goods Sold to include directly attributable handling/inbound shipping if not already capitalized into unit lot costs

log.answer:
Total units sold: 78 + 67 + 103 + 115 + 113 + 32 = 508 units.

All purchases occur before all sales, so perpetual and periodic FIFO are identical.

Lot exhaustion in order:
- Lot 1: 97 units @ $8.47 = $821.59
- Lot 2: 128 units @ $6.07 = $776.96
- Lot 3: 72 units @ $8.77 = $631.44
- Lot 4: 147 units @ $11.27 = $1,656.69
- Lot 5: 64 units @ $6.82 = $436.48 (balance: 508 - 444 = 64 units)

Per-sale transaction tracing verifies no rounding discrepancies:
- Sale 1 (78 units from Lot 1): 78 * 8.47 = $660.66
- Sale 2 (19 units Lot 1 + 48 units Lot 2): (19 * 8.47) + (48 * 6.07) = 160.93 + 291.36 = $452.29
- Sale 3 (80 units Lot 2 + 23 units Lot 3): (80 * 6.07) + (23 * 8.77) = 485.60 + 201.71 = $687.31
- Sale 4 (49 units Lot 3 + 66 units Lot 4): (49 * 8.77) + (66 * 11.27) = 429.73 + 743.82 = $1,173.55
- Sale 5 (81 units Lot 4 + 32 units Lot 5): (81 * 11.27) + (32 * 6.82) = 912.87 + 218.24 = $1,131.11
- Sale 6 (32 units Lot 5): 32 * 6.82 = $218.24

Total COGS = 660.66 + 452.29 + 687.31 + 1173.55 + 1131.11 + 218.24 = $4,323.16.

FINAL: 4323.16

asked: Total purchased units are 97+128+72+147+141+115+47+52 = 799 and total sold is 508 — confirm that cumulative sales never exceed cumulative receipts at any point in the stated sequence, and state the remaining inventory units after the final sale.

The lot-by-lot summary consumes Lots 1-4 in full (97+128+72+147 = 444) plus 64 units of Lot 5, yet the per-sale trace draws only 32+32 = 64 units from Lot 5 across sales 5 and 6 — confirm these two reconcile exactly and that no sale was mis-split at a lot boundary (specifically sale 4: 49 from Lot 3 leaves Lot 3 fully used at 23+49 = 72).
Does the reported total 4323.16 equal the lot-summary sum 821.59+776.96+631.44+1656.69+436.48 as well as the six per-sale subtotals? State both sums explicitly.
replies: All 8 lots are received before any sales occur ('It then sells, in this order...'). At the start of sales, cumulative receipts are 799 units. Cumulative sales reach 78, 145, 248, 363, 476, and finally 508 units, never exceeding 799. Remaining inventory is 799 - 508 = 291 units (77 units of Lot 5, plus all of Lots 6, 7, and 8: 77 + 115 + 47 + 52 = 291).

Reconciling lot usage across individual sales:
- Lot 1 (97 units): Sale 1 (78) + Sale 2 (19) = 97.
- Lot 2 (128 units): Sale 2 (48) + Sale 3 (80) = 128.
- Lot 3 (72 units): Sale 3 (23) + Sale 4 (49) = 72.
- Lot 4 (147 units): Sale 4 (66) + Sale 5 (81) = 147.
- Lot 5 (64 units drawn): Sale 5 (32) + Sale 6 (32) = 64.
Every sale boundary splits correctly and precisely reconciles with the lot-by-lot consumption of 444 + 64 = 508 units.
